title: Weekly sync - Serving Runtime / Infra / Console (agenda + action items)
content:
Meeting: Weekly cross-team sync - Serving Runtime / Infra / Console
Date: 2026-03-02
Time: 10:00 - 10:45 PT
Location: Zoom / #eng-serving-runtime channel
Owner / note-taker: Alex Chen
Attendees (expected): Alex Chen (owner), Priya Patel (infra), Samir Gupta (runtime), Maya Rivera (console), Jordan Lee (SRE), plus optional: performance-runbook group

Objectives:
- Surface blockers across runtime / infra / console that impact SLA/latency workstreams
- Align on short-term rollout plan for v2 batching and KV cache changes
- Track action items and owners; confirm next steps for observability gaps

Agenda (35 minutes total):
1) Quick updates (round-robin, 2 min each) — 10m
   - Infra: capacity changes, upcoming maintenance windows (Priya)
   - Runtime: v2 batching status, perf numbers (Samir)
   - Console: rollout of new per-route tracing UI (Maya)
   - SRE: incident triage and outstanding alerts (Jordan)

2) Deep-dive: v2 batching & KV cache rollout plan — 12m
   - Samir to present current perf delta and risk list
   - Priya to confirm infra capacity and canary window
   - Decide canary slice criteria and rollback triggers

3) Observability gaps & short-term fixes — 8m
   - Missing token-level cost breakdown in some routes (Maya)
   - Tracing sampling inconsistencies (Jordan)

4) AOB / parking lot / wrap-up — 5m

Notes / Discussion Highlights:
- Infra: Priya - cluster upgrade scheduled 2026-03-06 (non-disruptive) but there is a limited maintenance slot for one AZ; will reserve during low-traffic window. Capacity cushion reduced to 8% during upgrade. (Action: Priya to confirm exact start/end times and callout to customers if needed.)

- Runtime: Samir - v2 batching shows avg token latency improvement of ~18% in internal perf runs, 5–10% CPU uplift on small-seq workloads. KV cache integration tests revealed a race when cache-eviction intersects with async-prefetch; replicable in testbed. Proposed fix: serialize eviction vs prefetch for same keyspace.
   - Risk: small increase in tail latency for specific traffic patterns until fix deployed.

- Console: Maya - tracing UI rollout in staging is on track; a couple of UX bugs (filters reset on navigation) found. Also noticed missing token-cost breakdown for batched requests due to a change in the telemetry schema.

- SRE: Jordan - recent alert noise from autoscaler on one Dedicated pool; likely config drift after infra changes last week. Working with infra to pin autoscaler thresholds.

Decisions made:
- Canary for v2 batching will run at 3% traffic on one region for initially 48 hours, metrics checkpoint at 6h/24h/48h. Rollout schedule contingent on no >5% increase in p95 latency and no customer-facing errors.
- KV cache prefetch/eviction serialization fix to be merged to staging before canary.

Action items (tracked):
1) Priya Patel: Publish exact maintenance window for cluster upgrade and post notice to #prod-status and customer-notifications. Due: 2026-03-03. Status: in_progress.
2) Samir Gupta: Implement and test eviction vs prefetch serialization fix; open PR and attach perf baseline. Due: 2026-03-05. Status: in_progress. Linked: GITHUB PR placeholder https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/678.
3) Maya Rivera: Update telemetry pipeline mapping to include token-level cost breakdown for batched requests; validate with staging traces. Due: 2026-03-04. Status: open.
4) Jordan Lee: Investigate autoscaler config drift on Dedicated pool, propose pinned thresholds & rollback plan. Due: 2026-03-05. Status: open. JIRA: INFRA-482.
5) Alex Chen: Draft canary runbook (criteria, dashboards, rollback steps) and share with teams for review. Due: 2026-03-03. Status: in_progress. Confluence draft: /display/SERV/Serving+Runtime+Runbook.
6) All: Validate test traffic generator covers edge-case small-seq patterns that trigger KV race (owners: Samir + SRE). Due: 2026-03-06. Status: open.

Parking lot / follow-ups (for next sync):
- Longer-term: model variant routing policy changes and impact on batching efficiency (shadow experiment proposed).
- Explore longer-term telemetry schema versioning to prevent breaking consumer assumptions.

Risks / blockers to escalate:
- If eviction vs prefetch fix cannot be QA'd by 2026-03-05, canary must be delayed — this impacts Dedicated customer SLA commitments for March rollout.
- Reduced capacity cushion during infra upgrade (Priya) may require temporary rate-limiting for lower-tier routes; decision delegated to infra/product on 2026-03-03 if capacity <10%.

Next meeting: 2026-03-09 same time (10:00 PT). Proposed focus: canary kickoff/initial metrics + infra upgrade post-mortem checklist.

Quick checklist before next sync:
- [ ] Priya: publish maintenance window + customer notice
- [ ] Samir: merge eviction/prefetch fix to staging + attach perf numbers
- [ ] Maya: restore token-cost telemetry for batched routes
- [ ] Jordan: pin autoscaler thresholds (temp) and report back
- [ ] Alex: finalize canary runbook and share link

Notes to self (Alex):
- Pull perf dashboards for p50/p95/p99 and token-cost by route ahead of canary.
- Coordinate with growth/customer-success for any targeted notices to affected customers in canary region.
- Keep the runbook small and actionable; prefer an operations checklist over long text.

Document versioning / history:
- 2026-02-24 created initial draft for planning
- 2026-03-02 updated after sync meeting (notes + action items)
- 2026-03-03 minor edits: added linked artifacts and updated due dates

End of doc.
